gap: None of the results ChatGPT got turns the inverters' different surge claims (W or VA, with or without a hold time) into one 240 V figure, or says that The Solar Lab measured the EG4 6000XP's rated '12,000 W for about 3.5 s' surge at only 7.3–7.5 kW for 3–5 s.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited: the Franklin SubDrive/MonoDrive FAQ and the Franklin SubDrive Connect product page. I also scanned the titles of the other Franklin results, which are all SubDrive product pages and manuals. The two pages I read cover the drive's input voltage (190–260 VAC), the 1/2–5 hp range and soft start. Neither says anything about inverter or generator sizing, surge ratings or starting current. ChatGPT's answer only says to use a 'pure sine wave inverter with high surge capacity' and gives no numbers. No rival compares surge ratings across brands or uses a measured surge figure.
decides: It backs leading with the low-frequency transformer units (Sun Gold Power 6000W 48V and AIMS 6000 W). Their surge rating is about 18,000 W, which is about 75 A at 240 V. The EG4 6000XP is rated 12,000 W (50 A) on paper, but The Solar Lab measured about 7.5 kW (about 31 A at 240 V). For a motor start, that puts it below both low-frequency units and below the SPH6548P's rated 13,000 VA. The SPH6548P's figure is unmeasured and has no published hold time. One Victron MultiPlus-II gives 120 V only, so a 240 V well pump needs two units. The table footnote should carry this.

findings.label: Surge, rated vs measured (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: Rated 12,000 W for about 3.5 s; measured 7.3–7.5 kW for 3–5 s
findings.source_title: EG4 6000XP Off-Grid Inverter Review: Is it the Ultimate All-in-One Solar Power Solution? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab calls the measured result 'pretty much exactly what they advertised'. The measured figure is about 62% of the 12 kW rating. Dividing by 240 V gives about 50 A rated and about 31 A measured. The page names no author or date (©2026).

findings.label: Per-leg continuous limit
findings.value: 3,000 W per 120 V leg; both legs used for 240 V; 6,000 W total continuous
findings.source_title: EG4 6000XP Off-Grid Inverter Review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab also says it pushed the unit to 6.25 kW before it tripped. A 240 V well pump runs across both legs, so the 3,000 W per-leg limit matters only for 120 V pumps.

findings.label: Price and the surge spec on the retailer page
findings.value: $1,499.99 (the page also shows $1,629.99, without saying which is the regular price); the page gives 'Rated Output Power: 6,000W' and no surge figure
findings.note: The retailer product page does not list surge, so a shopper on that page sees no surge figure.

findings.label: Continuous vs peak
findings.value: 5,000 VA / 4,000 W continuous at 25 °C; 9,000 W peak; no peak duration given
findings.note: The output is 120 V only. The page says the unit 'supports parallel and three-phase configurations' and does not mention 120/240 V split phase. A 240 V pump therefore needs a second unit. 9,000 W at 120 V is 75 A on one leg, not a 240 V figure.

findings.label: Price, design and peak in the maker store listing
findings.value: $1,220 (compare-at $4,713); 'Low frequency'; 120 VAC or 240 VAC output; the product URL slug reads '6000w-peak-18000w'
findings.source_title: 6000W DC 24V/ 48V Split Phase Pure Sine Wave Inverter With Charger (Sun Gold Power)
findings.note: Read with storecheck.py search on the maker's Shopify store. In this read, 18,000 W appears only in the URL slug. Peak 18,000 W ÷ 240 V = 75 A, the same as the AIMS unit on our current page. When I tried to re-check the 20 s hold time on the product page, the store returned HTTP 429.

findings.label: Peak and motor rating
findings.value: $1,035 (compare-at $4,526); 'Rated Output Power: 6500W, Max Peak Power: 13,000VA'; no hold time and no loaded-motor HP stated
findings.source_title: 6.5KW 48V Split Phase Solar Inverter SPH6548P (Sun Gold Power)
findings.note: 13,000 VA ÷ 240 V ≈ 54 A, with no hold time given. On the same store, Sun Gold Power lists a 'loaded motor capacity' of 6 HP for its 8KW and 10KW SPH units and 4 HP for the 5000W unit, but gives no HP figure for the SPH6548P.

findings.label: Maker's own motor-HP rating (normalising aid)
findings.value: 8KW: 16,000 W peak, 6 HP loaded motor; 10KW: 20,000 W peak, 6 HP; 5000W 48V: 4 HP
findings.source_title: 10KW 48V Split Phase Solar Inverter (Sun Gold Power)
findings.note: Read from the storecheck search output for these sibling listings ($1,305 / $1,422 / $530). This is the only maker in the set that states surge as motor horsepower, the unit a well-pump buyer actually knows.

findings.label: Soft start depends on motor type (Franklin SubDrive)
findings.value: 'Two-wire motors do not have soft start ability'; the drive needs 190–260 VAC line voltage
findings.note: A rival page ChatGPT cited. It says the SubDrive lowers start-up current but gives no input amps or inverter/generator sizing. With a 2-wire motor, or with no drive at all, the inverter has to supply the full locked-rotor current.

findings.label: SubDrive Connect scope (rival page)
findings.value: 1/2–5 hp; single-phase 2-wire and 3-wire and three-phase motors; soft start; no input-current or generator/inverter sizing stated
findings.note: A cited rival page. I checked it for anything about surge or inverter sizing and found nothing.
